Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are presenting with gait and limb ataxia; to begin our investigation, can you describe exactly how your walking difficulties have progressed over time?

Additionally, could you tell me if you have any significant medical history that might be relevant to these symptoms?

REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count, Comprehensive Metabolic Panel, Vitamin B12, and Folate levels.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the lab results; the normal blood work helps rule out many metabolic and infectious causes. To better understand your ataxia, could you describe whether your symptoms worsen with exercise or fatigue, and do you experience any double vision or slurred speech?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The description of looking "drunk" and feeling clumsy, particularly on the right side, suggests a cerebellar or brainstem lesion; can you confirm if you have noticed any specific eye movements like nystagmus or double vision?

REQUEST IMAGES: Brain MRI with and without contrast.
REQUEST TEST: Serum paraneoplastic antibody panel (Anti-Hu, Anti-Yo, Anti-Ri).

text: The MRI findings are highly concerning for Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML), showing multifocal demyelinating lesions without enhancement, which contradicts the normal paraneoplastic antibody panel. To determine the underlying cause of this opportunistic infection, do you have any history of severe immunosuppression, such as HIV/AIDS, organ transplantation, or recent chemotherapy?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) on your MRI and your history of Crohn's disease treated with natalizumab is highly suspicious for PML induced by this medication. Given this strong association, do you know when your last dose of natalizumab was administered?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had a recent fever or major infection that I know of. The symptoms are mostly gait imbalance, limb ataxia, and weaker use of my right arm.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy.
